hotspots.whyItMatters: Knowing whether an install falls under UL 681 (burglar/holdup) vs. UL 365 (police-connected) is a classic which-standard question.
hotspots.cite: UL 681. Confirm section in your copy
hotspots.trap: Assuming every burglar alarm install is automatically UL 681-compliant just because it's 'monitored,' without checking the specific installation classification it claims.

hotspots.topic: Line security and circuit supervision grades
hotspots.whyItMatters: Burglar alarm circuits are graded by how hard they are to defeat or tamper with, a recurring theme across alarm standards.
hotspots.cite: UL 681. Confirm section in your copy
hotspots.trap: Treating 'supervised' as one blanket feature instead of a graded property tied to the specific grade of service being provided.

hotspots.whyItMatters: The type of premises drives which installation classification (and therefore which requirements) apply.
hotspots.cite: UL 681. Confirm section in your copy
hotspots.trap: Applying a residential-grade installation classification to a commercial/mercantile premises because the equipment 'looks the same.'
